code.originalText: Four-week review: mycobacterial cultures, airway clearance, bone density, grief therapy, and her choice about the opioid dose

text.paragraph: Four-week review: cultures, airway clearance, bone density, grief therapy, and the opioid dose. [S]

Ms. Barrett Browning returns four weeks after the consultation. She does airway clearance every morning and evening and finds it tiring but worth it: her sputum is down from about four to two tablespoons a day, and she has seen no blood for two weeks. She has had four grief therapy sessions by video and says it is the first time she has spoken of her brother aloud; the first two sessions were very hard. She sleeps a little better. She had her DXA scan last week. She asks whether she could try a lower morphine dose, now that the cough is easing and she is sleeping a little better, but she does not want to stop it and is afraid of the restlessness she remembers when a dose was late. [S]

tr.td: Fewer crackles at the left base; no wheeze
Engaged; tearful briefly when speaking of her brother; no suicidal ideation

Chronic cough with daily yellow sputum, occasional streaks of blood, and breathlessness on stairs, worse in winter, for several years after an illness with blood in the sputum about eight years ago; tuberculosis, nontuberculous mycobacteria and bronchiectasis to be distinguished
S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis at the consultation; it echoes her documented chest illness (D).

Non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis of the left lower lobe and lingula with chronic Haemophilus influenzae infection and mild airflow obstruction (Bronchiectasis Severity Index 3, mild); tuberculosis and nontuberculous mycobacterial disease excluded; synthetic modern diagnosis chosen for a historical chest illness whose cause is disputed
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the nature of her historical chest illness remains undetermined (R, disputed).

Long-term prescribed opioid therapy (oral morphine 20 mg a day for many years, for cough, sleeplessness and palpitations), with expected physiological dependence; no opioid use disorder on DSM-5-TR assessment
S — Synthetic modern problem anchored to her documented prescribed opium (D); tolerance and withdrawal on prescribed opioids do not count toward opioid use disorder.

Prolonged grief disorder after the drowning of her closest brother five years ago, with yearning, self-blame, avoidance of reminders of the sea, and depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 12); no suicidal ideation
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to her documented bereavement (D); not a claim about her real mental health.

list.item:
Bronchiectasis (J47.9). Responding to airway clearance: less sputum, no blood, CRP 4.1 mg/L. Mycobacterial cultures show no growth at four weeks. The sputum culture sent last week again grew a light growth of Haemophilus influenzae. [S]
Continue airway clearance twice daily.
Final cultures at the next visit.

Long-term opioid therapy: her request to reduce (Z79.891). No opioid use disorder; she wants a slow reduction because the cough and sleep are improving and she would rather not damp the cough. A reduction of about 10 percent with each step held at least four weeks is reasonable; she can pause or go back a step at any time, and nothing will be forced. [S]
Morphine solution 4.5 mL (9 mg) twice daily from today.
Call if restlessness, sweating or sleeplessness lasts more than a few days.
Prescription monitoring program checked: one prescriber, one pharmacy.

Prolonged grief disorder (F43.81). PHQ-9 10 from 12 after four sessions; no suicidal ideation. [S]
Continue weekly grief therapy.
Safety plan reviewed.

Vitamin D deficiency and bone health (E55.9). DXA Z-scores -1.4 at the spine and -1.1 at the femoral neck: within the expected range for age, at the low end, as expected with her low weight and indoor life. No drug treatment needed. [S]
Continue vitamin D3 1819 units daily; recheck at twelve weeks.
Weight-bearing exercise in the home program.
Calcium from food, about 1000 mg a day.

Follow-up: Three-month review with the final mycobacterial cultures, vitamin D, PHQ-9 and GAD-7, and a check on the first dose step. Emergency care for more than a few teaspoons of blood. Next scheduled visit 1845-06-15: three-month review: final mycobacterial cultures, vitamin D, mood, safety, and the opioid dose. [S]
